description: The server has received the request headers and the client should continue sending the request body, or ignore this response if the request is already finished.
To have a server check the request headers, a client must send Expect: 100-continue in its initial request and receive this response before sending the body.
The server agrees to switch to the protocol requested by the client in its Upgrade header.
This deprecated WebDAV response indicated that a request had been received and was still being processed without a final status available yet.
The server sends preliminary headers, commonly Link headers, so the client can begin preloading resources before the final response is ready.
The request succeeded. The meaning of the response depends on the method, such as returning a resource for GET or the result of an action for POST.
The request succeeded and created a new resource, commonly after a POST or PUT request.
The server received the request but has not acted on it yet, often because another process will handle it asynchronously.
The response metadata came from a transforming proxy or another copy and may differ from what the origin server returned.
The request succeeded, but there is no content to send in the response. Updated headers may still be useful to the client.
The request succeeded and the client should reset the document or view that submitted it.
The server is returning only the part of a resource requested by a Range header.
The response contains information about multiple resources when several different status results may apply.
A WebDAV response avoids listing the same internal collection members more than once.
The server fulfilled a GET request and returned a representation created by applying one or more instance manipulations.
The request has more than one possible response, so the user agent or user must choose one.
The requested resource has moved permanently to the URL provided in the response.
The requested resource is temporarily available at another URL, but the client should continue using the original URL in future requests.
The server directs the client to retrieve the requested resource from another URI using GET.
The resource has not changed since the client's cached version, so the client can continue using that cached response.
This deprecated response indicated that the resource had to be accessed through a proxy.
This reserved response code is no longer used; it appeared in an earlier version of HTTP.
The resource is temporarily available at another URI, and the client must repeat the request with the same method.
The resource has moved permanently to another URI, and the client must preserve the original request method.
The server cannot or will not process the request because it appears to contain a client error, such as malformed syntax or invalid framing.
The client must authenticate itself to receive the requested response. Despite its name, this usually means unauthenticated.
This code was intended for digital payment systems, but it is rarely used and has no standard convention.
The server understands the request but refuses to provide the resource because the client lacks permission or access.
The server cannot find the requested resource. The URL may be unknown, or the resource may not exist even though the endpoint is valid.
The server knows the request method, but the target resource does not support it.
The server cannot find a response representation that matches the criteria in the client's Accept headers.
The client must authenticate with the proxy before the proxy can forward the request.
The server timed out while waiting for the client to send a request.
The request conflicts with the current state of the server or resource, such as when simultaneous edits cannot be reconciled.
The requested resource was permanently removed and has no known forwarding address.
The server rejected the request because it requires a Content-Length header.
A condition in the client's request headers was not met by the server.
The request body is larger than the server is willing or able to process.
The requested URI is longer than the server is willing to interpret.
The format of the request data is not supported by the server.
The ranges requested by the client cannot be fulfilled, often because they are outside the target resource.
The server cannot meet the expectation specified by the request's Expect header.
The server refuses an attempt to brew coffee with a teapot, a playful status from the Hyper Text Coffee Pot Control Protocol.
The request was sent to a server that cannot produce a response for the scheme and authority in the request URI.
The request is well-formed but cannot be processed because it contains semantic errors.
The WebDAV resource being accessed is locked.
The request failed because a previous request on which it depended also failed.
The server is unwilling to process the request because it may be replayed.
The server refuses the request with the current protocol but may accept it after the client upgrades.
The origin server requires a conditional request to help prevent lost updates.
The client has sent too many requests in a given amount of time and is being rate limited.
The server will not process the request because one or more header fields are too large.
The requested resource cannot legally be provided, such as when access is blocked by a government order.
The server encountered an unexpected situation and has no more specific 5xx response to use.
The server does not support the request method or lacks the ability to fulfill the request.
A server acting as a gateway or proxy received an invalid response from the upstream server.
The server is not ready to handle the request, commonly because it is overloaded or undergoing maintenance.
A gateway or proxy did not receive a response from the upstream server in time.
The HTTP version used in the request is not supported by the server.
The server has an internal content-negotiation configuration error that creates a circular reference.
A WebDAV method could not complete because the server cannot store the required representation.
The server detected an infinite loop while processing the request.
The request declares an HTTP extension that the server does not support.
The client must authenticate to gain network access, commonly through a captive portal.
